BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE HIRDESH  ON THE 6 th OF OCTOBER, 2025  MISC. APPEAL No. 301 of 2009  SMT.BHAVANA SHARMA AND OTHERS  Versus  RAMNIWAS JATAV AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Sudesh Kumar Singh - Advocate for the appellants  Shri Badri Nath Malhotra- Advocate for respondent No.
 Shri Bal Krishna Agrawal- Advocate for respondent No.
 ORDER

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act filed by the appellants/claimants arising out of the award dated 01/12/2008 passed by First Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (hereinafter referred as "Claims Tribunal), Gwalior, District- Gwalior in Claim Case No.160/2007 on account of inadequacy of compensation and seeking enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: First Additional, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The date of accident, negligence and issue of liability are not in dispute, however, the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard is not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Tribunal in the case of death of Kishore Kumar Sharma due to motor accident, Claims Tribunal has awarded NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24772 2 MA-301-2009 compensation to the tune of Rs. 23,42,744/-with interest from the date of filing of claim application till its realization.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants contended that Claims Tribunal has committed an error in awarding compensation amount to the claimants and Tribunal has not minutely examined the evidence and documentary evidence available on record and wrongly awarded compensation amount and without considering the age of deceased-Kishore Kumar Sharma, wrongly adopted multiplier of "16".

It is further submitted that Tribunal has awarded Rs. 2000/- for funeral expenses Smt.Bhavana Sharma vs Ramniwas Jatav on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99429520/
1 and Rs. 5000/- under the head of pain and suffering which are meagre and Claims Tribunal has also erred in not adding future prospects in compensation amount.
Hence, it is prayed that reasonable amount of compensation may be awarded to the claimants.

5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent Nos. 5 and 3/ Insurance Company contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and argued in support of the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal.

6. Heard the arguments advanced by the counsel for the parties and perused the record of the Claims Tribunal.
7.
After hearing counsel for the parties, it is found that Claims Tribunal has erred in not adding future prospects on income of deceased i.e. Rs. 18,248/- per month.
In considered opinion of this Court, the just and proper amount of compensation be awarded by adding future prospects on NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:24772 3 MA-301-2009 income of deceased.

8. As regards loss of income including future prospects, in the light of judgment of National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700 , the claimants are entitled for loss of income including future prospects of 50% as the deceased was a Government Servant and was aged 38 years at the time of alleged accident.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi , 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, as per the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, even if age of the deceased is to be taken into account, multiplier of "15" should be applied by the Claims Tribunal instead of multiplier of "16".

entities.text: Sarla Verma and ors. Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD AM  Income Rs. 18,248 X 12  Future Prospects@50% Rs.1,09,488/-

Total Income Rs. 3,28,464/-
 Dependency 2/3 Rs.2,18,976/-
 Loss of Income Rs. 2,18,976 x
Other Heads:-

Loss of Consortium 40,000X3 Rs.1,20,000/-
 Loss of Estate and funeral expenses Rs.30,000/-
Total Compensation 10.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.34,34,640/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of Rs.
23,42,744/-.

Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:24772 4 MA-301-2009 additional sum of Rs.10,91,896/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

Smt.Bhavana Sharma vs Ramniwas Jatav on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99429520/
2 11.
In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.10,91,896/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
It is made clear that appellants shall not get interest from 13/05/2009 to 08/03/2025.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

12. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants- claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
13. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE Prachi Smt.Bhavana Sharma vs Ramniwas Jatav on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99429520/
